title: Apps print their tailnet URL, ending in the version: profile default, TAILNET_URL override
body:
Scaffolded apps now say where they are viewed beyond localhost, and the URL ends in the app's version. The host is a setting, not a constant.

- A new optional profile section, `[serving] tailnet_url`. The polarizetech profile names `https://joshuas-macbook-pro.tailc463ae.ts.net`; `example.toml` leaves it empty.

- A profile without a `tailnet_url` prints nothing.
- Existing apps are untouched, because `serve.py` belongs to the repo once it is written.
- CHANGELOG (Unreleased) and a PROTOCOL § 6 advice line are added. Nothing new is enforced by `check`.

title: Lay out replies from an editable template file
body:

title: Plan the gateway as the hub, and record hosting options
Hub phase 2: queues, deadlines, duplicates, stale processes
body:
Builds phase 2 of the hub plan, and brings in the plan itself (#19, which conflicted with #20 in one paragraph of `docs/mcp-clients.md`; both paragraphs are kept). Merging this marks #19 merged.

## What's in it
- **Queues and limits** (`research_mcp/hub/queue.py`): retrieval runs two at a time and the rest wait in order. A research request the pipeline turns away (`PIPELINE_MAX_RUNS`) waits in line and starts when a slot frees, for up to 2 h. Model calls are limited per provider across all runs in the pipeline process (OpenRouter 8, NEAR AI 4, local 1).
- **Memory pressure**: retrieval and research wait while less than 10 % of memory is free (`kern.memorystatus_level` on macOS, `MemAvailable` on Linux).
- **Reply deadline**: every `ask` answers within 45 s. Longer work replies `queued` (position and estimate, under the error contract) or `working`, carries on in the gateway, and leaves its result for `hub__result`.
- **Duplicate research** (`research_mcp/hub/overlap.py`): the same words, or a bge-m3 similarity of 0.92 or more, attaches to the request on the go instead of starting a second run. From 0.80 the run starts with a warning naming the other request. Without embeddings only exact matches attach.
- **Stale processes** (`research_mcp/hub/processes.py`): `hub__board` lists stdio gateways (each holding its own library copy), gateways older than the code, and orphaned upstreams. They're reported, never killed. On this Mac it currently finds five stdio gateways.
- **Ledger**: an `attached_to` column, added to the live database on open. Run updates reach every attached request.
- **Docs**: `docs/hub-plan.md` marks phases 1 and 2 built and records the 2026-10-28 decisions. `docs/mcp-clients.md` describes the queues and duplicates.

## Decisions applied
Code conflicts are not held: each session works in its own worktree (decided 2026-10-28). The plan's "held" for code conflicts is replaced by the existing mention of other sessions' work.

## Checks
- `tests/test_hub_phase2.py`: lanes, memory hold, deadline replies finishing into the ledger, a busy retrieval lane, a full pipeline queuing then starting, exact and paraphrase attaches, near-duplicate warnings, no-embeddings behaviour, ledger migration, stale-process parsing, and the one-at-a-time local model across runs.
- 400 tests pass; ruff and `pyright --pythonpath .venv/bin/python` are clean.

title: Hub phase 1: ledger, error contract, health, usage, ladders
body:
Builds phase 1 of the hub plan (`docs/hub-plan.md`, in #19).

## What's in it
- **Request ledger** (`data/pipeline/hub.sqlite`): every `ask` gets a `request_id` and a row (client, session, project, repo, route, specialist, question fingerprint, files named, status, timings, problems; for a research run, provider, tokens and cost once its calls pass through the gateway). New tools: `hub__status`, `hub__board`, `hub__result(id)`.
- **One error contract** on every non-success reply: `status`, `component`, `what_failed`, `impact`, `fallback_used`, `options`, `recommendation`, `retry_after`. The relay shows it first in plain words. Gateway tool errors, upstream errors and the bridge's "gateway is down" all carry it.
- **Health and circuit breakers** for the reranker, embeddings, paper library, model provider, verifier, upstream processes, GitHub and the corpus (3 failures, then skipped for 120 s, then probed), with the plan's labelled fallbacks.
- **Usage meters**: OpenRouter `/api/v1/key` + `/api/v1/credits` (balance, day/week/month spend, burn per day, run-out); NEAR AI reported as "needs a reporting token" until `~/.config/polarize/nearai-reporting.env` exists; Ollama up/installed/loaded. Adds `hub__usage` and a cached one-line readout under each relay.
- **Provider ladders** (`research_pipeline/ladder.py`, `config/hub.default.toml`): planning, extraction and writing go OpenRouter → NEAR AI direct → local `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`, skipping a rung that is failing or low (USD 1 or 95 %). Each move is logged in the run's notes and ladder log. Checking stays on the local verifier.

## Decisions (asked 2026-10-28)
- Code conflict: **worktrees**. Nothing is blocked; `ask` mentions recent code work on the same repo from another session and says to use your own worktree.
- Degraded fallbacks: **ask once per session per component**. The reply is `needs_decision`; the client passes `decisions={"<component>": "fallback"|"stop"}`, and that choice holds for the rest of the session.
- Session identity: **pass it, or the gateway infers it**. The bridge sends `X-Hub-Session`/`X-Hub-Project`; inferred sessions are marked in the ledger.
- Ladders and thresholds: **as proposed**.

## Limits
- Switching off only the reranker or only the embeddings needs `rerank`/`dense` flags on paper-fetch's `retrieve` tool. The gateway sends them as soon as the tool lists them; until then those two fall back to scholarly search, and the relay says so.
- Inside a running pipeline, ladder moves happen automatically and are labelled; only the pre-run check asks.
- Upstream restart with backoff is phase 3: for now a dead upstream fails with the restart command.
- `docs/hub-plan.md` should record these decisions once #19 merges; for now they are in `docs/mcp-clients.md`.

## Checks
- `tests/test_hub.py`: fault injection for every component, plus the ledger, breakers, meters, ladders and the gateway's hub tools.
- 388 tests pass; ruff and `pyright --pythonpath .venv/bin/python` are clean.

title: Over-fetch four passages, not three times the limit
body:
`rag__retrieve_evidence` asked the paper library for `limit * 3` passages so that passages excluded by the safety scan would not shrink the result. The library reranks three candidates per passage asked for, on the CPU, at about 0.3 s each. So a default request (limit 8) reranked 72 candidates, about 20 s, and under concurrent load that timed out clients' 60 s MCP calls. Asking for `limit + 4` keeps a margin for excluded passages at a fraction of the cost.

This has been running on the live gateway since 2026-10-27. Tests pass (351), and ruff and pyright are clean.

title: Start studies and tools exploratory, from a goal and a rough approach

The person's requirement (2026-10-28): studies and tools start exploratory by default, with "a general goal" and a "rough idea of how we might get there" instead of a strict claim. The first conversation is a back-and-forth to decide whether the goal fits one study or tool, or should be broken up.

- **A tool:** `scaffold new tool <name> --goal "..." --approach "..."` (or `--job`) writes an exploratory `SCOPE.toml` with the same fields.
- **Sizing:** both record the decision as `scope = "one"` or `"split: a, b"` with `scope_decided`. `scaffold check` warns until it is there and fails on another value.

title: Send every question to the retrieval tool, and let it pick the specialist

title: Add ask: one entry point that routes a request and runs only what it needs
body:
The goal: run research and code from the gateway, with the chat model of choice relaying what it did, and without overdoing it on each request.

- **`ask(question, repo?, mode?, strictness?)`.** A built-in gateway tool. The server instructions tell clients to start every request with it and to show its `relay` unchanged.
- **Routing** (`research_mcp/routing.py`) uses trigger words, not a model. Defaults are in `config/routing.default.toml`; the operator's own go in a gitignored `config/routing.toml`, which is re-read on every call.
  - `quick` (the default): one retrieval of five passages.
  - `research`: an evidence question; starts the research pipeline.
  - `code`: a task on code or a code review. A question never recruits the coder, even about code.
  - Prefixes force a route: `quick:`, `research:`, `deep:`, `code:`, `review:`.
  - A plain code task skips retrieval, because the library holds papers, not code (about 10 s down to 0.1 s live).
- **The specialist** comes from `agent_profiles.route`, or from the operator's `[profiles]` words.
- **The relay block** says what ran and why, lists the passages with their evidence ids, gives the specialist's guidance, and ends with a Limits line.
- **The gateway does not make code changes itself yet.** On the code route it gives context and names the `repos__` tools.

title: Harden repos__propose_files and allow a dedicated GitHub token
body:
Prepares the `repos__` tools for use from a chat client (Open WebUI) whose model may have read untrusted text, such as paper passages or web pages.

## What changes

- **`repos__propose_files` refuses dangerous paths** before anything is cloned:
  - Any path with a `.git` component. Writing `.git/config` can set `core.fsmonitor` or similar settings, so the next `git add` would run a program on the host.
  - `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/`. A workflow on a pushed branch runs with the repository's secrets before anyone reviews the PR.
  - Writing through a symbolic link.
  - Paths are compared case-insensitively, since macOS would place `.GitHub/Workflows/x.yml` inside `.github/workflows/`.
- **Every git command** runs with `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and `core.fsmonitor=false`. Credentials come explicitly from `gh auth git-credential`, so the tool no longer depends on the host's global git config.
- **`GITHUB_MCP_TOKEN_FILE`** (optional) gives the tool its own token, for example a fine-grained token limited to chosen repositories with Contents and Pull requests read/write and no Workflows permission. It is passed to `gh` and git as `GH_TOKEN`, and errors name the file, never the token. Without it, behaviour is unchanged: `gh`'s login is used.
- **`repos__auth_status`** reports the credential source (`gh login` or `GITHUB_MCP_TOKEN_FILE`) and the protected paths.
- **Docs:** `config/rag.env.example` and `docs/mcp-clients.md` describe the token file and the protected paths. They also note the remaining exposure: a workflow that already runs on every push still runs proposed code with whatever secrets it can reach, so deploy secrets belong in GitHub environments that require approval.

## Testing

- 15 new tests: rejected and allowed paths, refusing symlinks, path checks running before any command, token-file handling and errors, and the git hardening flags.
- The full suite passes locally (325 tests). Ruff is clean.
- Checked with a fake token that `gh auth git-credential` returns `GH_TOKEN`.
- The running gateway serves this code. `repos__auth_status` and `repos__list_repositories` work. `propose_files` has not been run against a real repository.

title: Bench sims: scaffold new sim --reference, checks and make sims
body:
**Depends on #5 (`tool-comparison-units`).** This branch is built on it, so the diff against `main` includes #5's commits (02841dc, bdd5dbc) until #5 merges. Review only the last two commits: 42157bf and 35f6117.

Protocol: polarizetech/adaptive-preregistration#3 (TOOL_VERSIONING.md §1b).

## What it adds
- `scaffold new sim <name> -q "..." --inside <tool> --reference "NAME=OWNER/REPO@TAG[#SUBDIR],licence=L[,runs=process][,package=P][,commit=SHA][,command=C]"` creates a **bench sim** in `sims/<name>`:
  - It resolves the tag's commit with `git ls-remote`.
  - It refuses a branch, an unstated licence, and GPL code that would be imported.
  - It renders the sim from `templates/units/bench`:
    - `SCOPE.toml`, with `kind = "bench"` and `[[references]]`;
    - its own `pyproject.toml`, which pins each imported reference as `pkg @ git+URL@TAG#subdirectory=...`;
    - an undecided `tolerances.toml`;
    - `run.py`, which refuses to score before the tolerances are decided and committed, or against a reference at another commit. It fetches process references into an ignored cache and writes `results/<tool version>.json`;
    - a pytest wrapper.
  - It registers the sim under `[[comparisons]]` with `kind = "bench"`.
- `scaffold check` fails when:
  - a reference is pinned to a branch or has no full commit;
  - a reference is missing from the sim's `pyproject.toml`, or pinned there at another tag, repo or subdirectory;
  - a bench sim has no `tolerances.toml`, or has results from before the tolerances were decided;
  - the latest result was scored against tolerances that have since changed;
  - a bench sim has a `preregistrations/` folder.

  It warns when GPL code is imported.
- Tool `Makefile`:

title: Share one half-precision vector copy; allow hosted embeddings and reranking
body:
## Why
Each process held its own float32 copy of every passage vector (665 MB at 164k passages). With one MCP server per Claude session, that exhausted memory and retrieval timed out.

## What
- **Shared vectors.** The vectors are written once as a float16 `.npy` beside the index (`<index>.vectors/`), memory-mapped read-only, and shared by every process through the page cache (336 MB). Scoring widens one 16k-row block at a time, so a query never holds a float32 copy.
- **Fresh across processes.** The copy is named by (count, max id, sum of ids) of the vectors it holds and is checked when `pragma data_version` changes. A paper indexed by another process is now found by dense search without a restart, which was a bug before. Writes are atomic renames, and superseded copies are removed only when older.
- **Hosted models, optional.**
  - `PAPER_FETCH_EMBED_API=openai` (the default when the URL ends in `/v1`) uses an OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings` endpoint. `PAPER_FETCH_EMBED_MODEL` stays the index's model identity; `PAPER_FETCH_EMBED_API_MODEL` is the provider's name for it.
  - `PAPER_FETCH_RERANK_URL` uses a Cohere/Jina-style `/rerank` endpoint.
  - Keys come from `*_KEY` or `*_KEY_FILE`. Both stay off unless configured.

## Tested
- 385 tests pass, including new ones: the shared file is mapped by a second index, a writer's new passages are seen by a reader, float16 keeps the top-10 ranking, a read-only location falls back to an in-process copy, and the hosted embedder and reranker accept the common answer shapes.
- Live on the 164k-passage index behind the shared gateway: retrieval 8–12 s warm. The process footprint is 1.6 GB, mostly the ONNX reranker; the vectors are a shared mapped file.
- The hosted providers have not been tried against a real service yet.

title: Endpoint providers: configured provider by default, cheapest zero-retention first, Near AI support
body:
## What

**Cheapest zero-retention provider first (OpenRouter).** A new setting, `PIPELINE_ENDPOINT_SORT`, defaults to `price` and adds `provider.sort` next to `zdr`. For Qwen3.8 27B, OpenRouter then routes to Near AI, at about 1.3¢ per research question instead of about 2.2¢ with load balancing. It falls back to the next zero-retention provider on failure.

**Near AI as a direct provider** (`https://cloud-api.near.ai/v1`, model `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`), for spending prepaid Near AI credits:
- Each call's cost is computed from Near AI's public model list. `PIPELINE_ENDPOINT_PRICE` sets prices for any other host that doesn't report cost. An unknown cost is logged as unknown, not zero.
- Run logs name the provider.
- A 402 or credit/balance error says the host may be out of credits.

**The configured provider is the default in the research tool too.** `PIPELINE_MCP_LLM` and `PIPELINE_LLM` now default to `auto`, meaning the configured endpoint when one is set, else the calling model (MCP) or Ollama (CLI). Nothing changes for anyone without an endpoint. `research_start(model="client")` hands one run to the calling assistant when the user asks it to do the writing itself. Replies report `model_backend`, and the gateway's instructions to assistants were updated to match.

Live check through the research tool's own `research_start`/`research_continue` with the real config: the run used the endpoint, handed no tasks to the caller, made 60 calls on zero-retention providers (mostly Near AI) with 0 reasoning tokens, cost 1.3¢ and finished in about 5 minutes.

**`web__search` is listed only when SearXNG is configured.** Without it the tool could only fail, and clients kept calling it. If called anyway, it now explains the fallback: the client searches the web itself and passes the URLs to `papers__leads`. Across 265 runs the web fallback was wanted in 1.2% of searches, so no search engine is required.

**Retries on dropped connections.** Dropped connections and failed TLS handshakes are retried with jittered backoff, up to `PIPELINE_ENDPOINT_RETRIES` (default 8).

**No personal paths in code.** `github_mcp` and `patent_mcp` no longer hardcode a home directory. They check the environment variable, then PATH, then `~/.local/bin`.

The docs gain a providers table comparing OpenRouter with Near AI direct, and a cost comparison against renting or buying a GPU.

## Near AI direct: not reliable today

On 2026-10-26, Near AI's API dropped 20–65% of connections during the TLS handshake. Failures rose with parallelism, and all of them came from its single address. Two real research runs failed, the second after one call failed 8 times in a row. Through OpenRouter, the same Near AI-hosted model answered every call. OpenRouter therefore stays the documented default, and Near AI direct is an option.

## Privacy

I scanned tracked files and history for API keys, tokens, emails, home paths and env/key files. Nothing secret was found. The plugin manifests intentionally name the author, with an info@ address, and the public MCP host URL.

## Tests

297 pass. New tests cover the provider default and per-run override, Near AI pricing, the provider label, configured prices, the out-of-credits message and connection retries. Pyright and ruff are clean.

title: Add an OpenAI-compatible endpoint backend for the text model
body:
## What

The research pipeline's text model can now run on any OpenAI-compatible chat API (OpenRouter, Fireworks, vLLM, Ollama's `/v1`). It's for research runs that should stay off a hosted assistant. Only the text model moves. Embeddings, the reranker and a configured local verifier (MiniCheck) stay on this machine.

- `Endpoint` in `research_pipeline/llm.py`:
  - Reasoning is off by default (`reasoning: {effort: "none"}`). A model that rejects this is retried with reasoning on, and the run log says so.
  - On OpenRouter, every request carries `provider: {zdr: true}`. Calls go only to zero-retention providers or fail.
  - Answers are requested as `json_schema` and validated against the schema, with one corrected retry. The request falls back to `json_object` if a host rejects `json_schema`.
  - Rate limits and upstream errors are retried with backoff.
- Settings: `PIPELINE_ENDPOINT_URL`, `_MODEL`, `_KEY` / `_KEY_FILE`, `_REASONING`, `_ZDR`, `_CONCURRENCY`. Use `PIPELINE_LLM=endpoint` for the CLI and benchmarks; `PIPELINE_MCP_LLM` now also accepts `endpoint`. **The MCP default stays `client`.**
- The run log records the served model version, the provider, tokens (including reasoning tokens) and cost.
- `eval_pipeline.py` takes `--backend`, `--model` and `--label`, and shows a cost column.

## Model choice

Docs now recommend **`qwen/qwen3.8-27b` as the default** and **`moonshotai/kimi-k3` for important questions**, with `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` as a backup. These come from a comparison on the 4 regression cases: offline, reasoning off, all calls on zero-retention providers.

| Model | Passed | Declined unanswerable | Cost per question |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8 27B | 2/4 | yes | ~1.7¢ |
| Kimi K3 | 2/4 | yes | ~14¢ |
| DeepSeek V4 Pro | 2/4 | yes | ~3.4¢ |
| GLM-5.2 | 1/4 | no | ~4¢ |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 1/4 | no | ~1.2¢ |
| Claude Opus 5.5 (reference) | 1/4 | no | ~55¢ |

4 cases is a smoke test, not an accuracy estimate. The full notes are in `docs/research-pipeline.md`.

## Fixes found while benchmarking

- Two runs of one question started in the same second wrote to the same run folder, and one overwrote the other. Run folders are now claimed atomically with a numeric suffix.
- Local verifier calls under the endpoint backend were missing from the run log's call list.
- The `must_not_claim` pattern `\bcauses?\b` matched "all-cause mortality", so every model failed on wording. It now excludes `all-`.

title: Ask the caller to search the web when the library cannot
body:
## Summary

The last resort after the scholarly providers is a web search. Until now that needed a hosted SearXNG instance; without one, the fallback was skipped.

paper-fetch runs no language model, but its caller is usually a model with its own web search. This PR hands the last step to the caller, so nothing needs hosting.

- **`ask_the_web` in search results.** When the fallback is wanted (no open-access hit) and the library's own web search did not answer, the result carries `ask_the_web` with `why`, the `query`, what happened to the library's own web search, and `how` to proceed. "Did not answer" means `SEARXNG_URL` is unset or SearXNG is down.
- **`leads`**, available as `Library.leads`, the MCP `leads` tool and `paper-fetch leads <url> ...`. It takes the URLs the caller found. It reads a DOI, PMID, PMCID or arXiv id out of each, using the web provider's own parser, marks what is already held, and returns what to `fetch`. It makes no network calls. A URL with no identifier is returned under `no_identifier` rather than dropped.
- **MCP instructions** tell the model what to do when it sees `ask_the_web`.

The rule is unchanged: nothing is downloaded from a web page. An identifier goes through the open-access providers, which decide whether a copy may be kept.

SearXNG still works when configured, and then nothing is asked of the caller. `web_fallback=False` and `PAPER_FETCH_WEB_FALLBACK=0` turn off the request along with the fallback.

title: Wait out a provider's outside problems; flag its defects
body:
## Summary

A search already asks every provider and merges whatever answers, with web search last. This PR fixes how a *failing* provider is treated, by telling two kinds of failure apart.

**An outside problem** means the service is down, rate-limiting us or out of allowance.
- The provider is reported as `unavailable` and the other providers answer.
- The provider is then left alone for a while instead of being asked again by every search:
  - 60 s after an outage
  - 300 s after a 429
  - an hour after OpenAlex's daily allowance
  - the rest of the process after scite's monthly one
- While paused it isn't called. Its report says `unavailable` with `paused: true` and the original reason.
- A cached answer is still served, and `refresh=True` asks anyway.

**A defect** means the service rejected our request or its answer changed shape. Waiting won't fix it, so:
- It is never paused.
- Its report says `error` with `broken: true`.
- The search result carries a top-level `broken` list.
- The CLI prints `! BROKEN: …` on stderr.
- The MCP server's instructions tell the model to tell the user.
- The traceback is logged to a local file, shown by `paper-fetch problems --trace`.

## The bug this fixes

Nine query helpers did `if r.status != 200: return []`. A provider answering 500, or rejecting a malformed query with 400, was reported as **`ok`, 0 hits**, so an outage or a bug read as "nothing in the literature".

They now go through `Provider._answered`, which raises one kind of failure or the other. It applies only to query endpoints, which answer 200 with an empty list when nothing matches. A lookup by identifier can still treat a 404 as "not known".

## Also in this PR

- **scite:** its failures are sorted the same way. A spent allowance or a busy service is unavailable. A rejected request, a JSON-RPC error, an unrecognised tool error or an answer without `hits` is a defect.
- **OpenAlex:** a 429 or 5xx is unavailable rather than a generic error.
- **Locating copies:** a defect met while locating a copy is logged too.
- **README install lines:** they used a PyPI name that doesn't exist (404). They now install from this repository.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest`: 367 passed, 96% coverage. Five existing tests relied on a 404 meaning "empty" and now use real empty answers.
  - `tests/test_fallbacks.py` covers pausing, the pause lengths, cache served while paused, defects named and logged, and web search asked when every provider is down.
  - `tests/test_providers.py` checks that all eight query providers treat a 503 or 403 as unavailable and a 400 as broken.
  - `tests/test_scite.py` covers the scite classification.
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pyright` are clean.
- [x] Live: five searches in one process. All nine default providers answered `ok`, including for a nonsense query, so none had been failing silently. scite reported its spent allowance once and was reported as paused on the next search. Zero defects were logged.

title: One Library, many threads: lock the catalogue, memory, collections and pacing
body:
Follow-up to #8. An MCP server runs every tool call on a worker thread, so one `Library` is used from several threads at once. #8 locked the passage index's connection. This PR covers the rest of the state those threads share.

- **Catalogue:**
  - One lock guards the in-memory dictionary and its save.
  - Readers that walk the catalogue take a snapshot (`_rows()`). Writers go through `_record` / `_forget`.
  - A save now updates the dictionary in place without emptying it. Before, a lookup from another thread mid-save could find a held paper missing and fetch it again.
  - `rebuild_index` builds the new catalogue aside and swaps it in whole.
- **Search memory and collections:** each read-modify-write holds a lock, so no thread's row or member is lost.
- **Lazily built parts** (profiles, memory, passage index, reranker): built once.
- **Provider request spacing:** two threads could both pass the wait at once and break a rate limit such as PLOS's 10 per minute. The wait is now taken under a per-provider lock.

No lock is held across a fetch or a search, so slow network work does not block other calls. The locks are per process; the cross-process behaviour is unchanged.

**Tested:**
- `tests/test_threads.py` runs each part from 16 threads. All five tests fail on main and pass here.
- The thread tests passed 25 runs in a row.
- All 324 tests pass, and ruff and pyright are clean.

title: Lock the passage index's connection: tool calls run on worker threads
body:
**What failed:** `retrieve` failed intermittently in service. The gateway log shows 13 failed calls. Eleven are `sqlite3.InterfaceError: bad parameter or other API misuse`, and one is passage text read back as undecodable bytes.

**Cause:** the MCP library runs every sync tool on a worker thread (`anyio.to_thread.run_sync`), so overlapping `retrieve` calls used the passage index's single SQLite connection at the same time. The index was written as if calls were serial.

**Fix:** `PassageIndex` holds an `RLock` around every use of its connection, including reads, writes and the cached vector matrix. Embedding, the slow part of indexing, stays outside the lock, so indexing a paper does not block retrieval for seconds.

title: Add scite as a search provider, through its MCP server
body:
## Summary

Adds **scite** as a search provider alongside OpenAlex and the others. It uses your scite subscription and needs no API key.

scite's REST search (`/api_partner/search`) returns 401 without a partner token, which comes from their sales team. Its MCP server (`https://api.scite.ai/mcp`) accepts the subscriber's own sign-in instead: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. So the provider is a small MCP client written against `Http`. It sends `initialize`, then `tools/call search_literature`.

## What changes

- **Sign-in:** `paper-fetch scite-login` opens the browser once and stores the sign-in in `~/.config/paper-fetch/scite-oauth.json` (mode 0600). It is never written to the shared store. `scite-logout` removes it.
- **Token renewal:** the access token is renewed automatically. scite rotates the refresh token on every use, so the file is re-read before a refresh and once more after a refused one.
- **Provider:** `providers/scite.py` is search-only, like `doaj`. It is in the default search set and reported `skipped` until someone signs in. Its results are not cached.
- **What a hit keeps:** DOI, title, year, three authors, scite's open-access flag and status, the citation tally and editorial notices.
- **What a hit drops:** scite's access links (they carry the account's email address), abstracts and citation statements.
- **Merged search results:** a hit that scite found carries a `scite` key with the tally, `oa_status` and `editorial_notices`.
- **HTTP layer:** `Http.post` is new. It returns a 4xx response as an answer, the way `get` does. `http.py` stays the only module that calls `urlopen`.
- **Docs:** README, `CLAUDE.md` and `INTEGRATION.md` are updated.

## Design notes

- **No `mcp` SDK in the core.** The core stays standard-library plus pypdf, and all outbound requests still go through `Http`. The one new socket is the loopback listener that receives the browser redirect during login.
- **`oa_only`:** the tool has no open-access filter. The provider asks for three times `limit` (capped at 50, because every hit carries a citation list) and drops what scite marks closed.
- **Failures:** an expired sign-in, a 429, a tool error or an unreachable server is reported as `unavailable` with what to do, never as zero results.

`quality.spectrum()` promised to summarise Goertzel bins into display buckets, but evaluated only every `step`-th DFT bin and skipped the rest. On a record longer than a couple of seconds a narrow line fell between the evaluated bins and disappeared. A 260-count 10 Hz sine in noise over 20 s drew its tallest point at 35.65 Hz, about 1.7 counts. The Monitor tab's spectrum (`POST /spectrum`, up to 20 s every ~500 ms) was affected the same way.

## The fix

- Every transform bin in the range is evaluated, and each bucket reports the **maximum** amplitude of the bins it covers. A maximum keeps a narrow line at its own amplitude however long the record is; a mean of power would dilute it. The price, stated in the docstring: the noise floor of the display rises slowly with record length, and it is not a power density.
- Cost: one stdlib radix-2 FFT of the Hann-windowed record, zero-padded to the next power of two at or above twice its length, over at most the most recent 16,384 samples (65 s at 250 Hz). The padding bounds the scalloping loss at 4 %.
- `freqs` are now bucket centres. `resolution_hz` keeps its meaning (rate / samples used). New fields: `bucket_hz`, `bin_hz`, `samples_used`, `summary`. The web client needs no change.

| Record | Tallest point | Amplitude (input 260) | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 s | 10.01 Hz | 259.5 | 3 ms |
| 20 s | 9.97 Hz | 256.8 | 56 ms |
| 60 s | 9.98 Hz | 257.0 | 119 ms |

## Checks

- `apps/server/dev_check.py`: a 10 Hz sine in noise at 2 s, 20 s and 60 s must be the tallest point, within one bucket of 10 Hz and within 10 % of the input amplitude; plus a check on the sample cap.
- `python3 scripts/check.py`: all seven suites pass. `check_docs.py` run against the blog post: in step. ruff clean.

## Versioning

No version bump and no `model-v*` tag. `quality.py` is in the measuring chain, but `spectrum()` feeds only the drawing: nothing it returns is stored in a session or an export, and `assess()` and `bands()` are unchanged. The CHANGELOG entry says so. If this should be 0.2.1 instead, that is a follow-up commit here.

title: Do not index reference lists that have no heading paragraph
body:
Found in a live run of retrieval-augmented-generation: a bibliography entry from a PDF was retrieved as a passage. The chunker only cut at a paragraph that was exactly "References". PDF text often has the heading on a line inside a paragraph, or loses it altogether.

**Detection** (`references_start`)
- A heading on a line of its own ("References", "6. References", "Literature Cited"), past the first third of the text.
- Or, with no heading: a run of at least 8 consecutively numbered entries starting at 1 that begins in the second half of the text, reaches its last tenth, and mostly carries publication years.
- Numbered lists in the body are kept. That covers lists that are short, early, have no years, or do not start at 1.

**Measured on 80 held papers:** 11 of 12 PDFs are now cut (none were before), every cut I read lands at the start of the list, and the 68 JATS and TEI texts are unaffected. An unnumbered author-year list with no heading is still not recognised.

**Existing indexes**
- The chunker has a version (`CHUNKER = 2`), kept in a new `chunked` table next to the `indexed_at` of the row it describes.
- The `papers` table is unchanged, so servers still running older code and sharing the file keep working. A paper one of them re-indexes counts as stale again.
- `has()` is false for a stale paper, so it is re-chunked the next time it is indexed. Passages whose text did not change keep their vectors, so only new text is embedded.
- `status` reports `stale`.

**Tested:** 287 tests pass, including the detector's positive and negative cases, vector reuse, an index from before versions existed, and a row rewritten by older code. ruff and pyright are clean.

title: A verifier call with no answer fails that check, not the run
body:
Found by a live run. One verify call generated 16,000 tokens without ever closing its JSON answer, hit the 600 s wall-clock limit, and ended the whole run. It happened twice.

- **Output cap:** every structured call is capped by `PIPELINE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (default 2048), so a runaway call stops in about a minute.
- **Narrower error:** `ModelOutputError`, a subclass of `LLMError`, marks one failed call: out of time or tokens, or not JSON. An unreachable server or a client that stopped answering still raises `LLMError` and ends the run.
- **Failed checks:** a verifier call that fails this way is recorded as `CHECK_FAILED` and never counts as support.
- **Unverified claims:** a claim that no verifier answered for gets `VERIFIER_FAILED`. It is removed from the answer and counted in Limits. A real verdict from another check still decides the claim.

title: Hand searching and indexing to paper-fetch
body:
Phase 3 of splitting the work between the two repositories. [paper-fetch](https://github.com/polarizetech/paper-fetch) now owns everything about finding and indexing papers (polarizetech/paper-fetch#2, #3, #4). This repository tells it the field and the concepts, then does everything after a passage is found: reading it, judging it, and checking the claims made from it.

**Changes**
- **Search:** `search` takes the domain's discipline profile (paper-fetch's profile with the same slug) and an optional collection (`--collection`, `PIPELINE_COLLECTION`, or `research_start(collection=)`). Searches are remembered, and the run log lists earlier searches on the same concept.
- **Planning:** the planner reads the profile's indexed terms, measures and search guidance. If the library has no such profile, the run says so.
- **Fetching:** the library's `relevance()` decides the fetch order, and the library indexes the fetched texts.
- **Retrieval:** passages come from the library's `retrieve()`, with stable ids (`<work>#p<ord>`) and the paper's metadata. `Evidence.passage_id` is now that string id.
- **Removed:** `index.py`, the embedding calls, the ONNX reranker, and the numpy dependency. The local-model reranker stays. Study-design notes move to `notes.sqlite`, keyed by the text hash.
- **Domains:** each keeps its evidence half (taxonomy, measures, critique rules, prompt rules). Anchors, sources and search guidance are now paper-fetch profiles, and `DomainPolicy.profile` names the profile to use. The domain template ships a `profile.toml`, and `DOMAINS.md` explains both halves.
- **Gateway:** the `rag__` tools read and index through the paper library's MCP session. Evidence ids keep the same format.

**Tests**
- 225 tests pass, and ruff and pyright are clean.
- The tests run against a real in-memory paper-fetch `Library`. It's a test-only dependency, pinned to a commit that is now on paper-fetch's main.
- The gateway tests run paper-fetch's real MCP server as the upstream, with every proxy pointed at a closed port so nothing can reach the network.
- New tests check that the profile reaches the planner, that profile and collection reach search, fetch and retrieval, and that a missing profile is noted.

**Live migration (already done locally)**
- The old index (735 papers, 33,852 passages, bge-m3 vectors) was copied into paper-fetch's index without re-embedding. Re-splitting six sampled texts reproduced their passages exactly, and the text hashes matched.

title: Passage index and retrieval
body:
Phase 2 of moving paper searching and indexing into paper-fetch. This PR is stacked on #2 (the base is `search-profiles-collections`), so merge #2 first.

**What moves here from retrieval-augmented-generation**
- The passage index (`passages.py`). It is a local SQLite file built from held full texts, with FTS5 (BM25) always and dense vectors when `PAPER_FETCH_EMBED_MODEL` is set, fused by reciprocal rank.
- Chunking and hidden-character cleaning are unchanged, so passage offsets and `text_sha256` mean what they did in the RAG index. The paper row now also records how many hidden characters were removed (`hidden_chars`).
- Passage ids have the form `<work>#p<ord>` and survive rebuilds. `sha` identifies the passage text.
- The ONNX cross-encoder reranker (`rerank.py`), set with `PAPER_FETCH_RERANK_MODEL`.
- The embedder and the reranker are both deterministic: they return vectors and scores, never text. The model-based reranker and the prompt-injection scan stay in the application, because both concern a model reading the text.

- `Library.retrieve(queries, identifiers=, collection=, limit, per_paper, rerank)` indexes its scope on demand before retrieving.

- New optional extras: `retrieval` (numpy) and `rerank` (onnxruntime, tokenizers, huggingface_hub). The core still depends only on pypdf and fonttools.

title: Discipline profiles, named collections and search memory
body:
Phase 1 of moving paper searching and indexing out of retrieval-augmented-generation and into paper-fetch. Nothing here uses a language model: everything is string matching and bookkeeping, so it is repeatable and tested offline.

**Discipline profiles** (`profiles.py`, data in `profile_data/*.toml`)
- A profile holds the search half of a field: controlled terms (MeSH ids are validated), synonyms, measures, sources, and search guidance for whoever writes the queries.
- `search(profile=)` also runs up to two variants that swap a synonym for its indexed term ("HRV" → "heart rate variability"). It never swaps the other way. Hits whose titles name the field's terms rank first (`profile_match`), and results are merged across variants (`found_by`).
- Four profiles ship built in. They were converted from the RAG repo's domains. They don't narrow the provider set, because that would drop the repository providers that find open copies.
- A TOML file in `~/.config/paper-fetch/profiles/` adds a profile or replaces a built-in one by slug.

**Named collections** (`collection.py`)
- `papers/collections/<name>.json` holds a member list and a default profile. A paper is stored once, whichever collections list it.
- `fetch(collection=)` lists the paper in the collection. `collect` and `uncollect` add or remove members by any identifier.

**Search memory** (`memory.py`)
- `papers/memory/searches.jsonl` gets one row per search, written with the same re-read-and-append approach as the catalogue.
- Every search reports up to three earlier searches on the same concept, and marks each hit that an earlier search already found (`seen_before`).
- `recall` looks up past searches by concept, profile, collection or paper. A concept is the set of content words with synonyms mapped to indexed terms.

**Surfaces**
- New MCP tools: `profiles`, `recall`, `collections`, `collection`, `create_collection`, `collect`, `uncollect`. `search` and `fetch` take `profile` and `collection`.
- New CLI commands: `profiles`, `collection`, `collect`, `recall`, plus `--profile` and `--collection` on `search` and `fetch`.

**Tested:**
- 239 tests pass offline, including concurrent writers to the memory and to a collection. ruff and pyright are clean.
- A live search with the cardiovascular profile, run on an in-memory store, found the "heart rate variability" variant hits, ranked them first, and recalled the earlier "HRV" search at a score of 0.8.

**Next:**
- Phase 2: the passage index and retrieval move here.
- Phase 3: retrieval-augmented-generation calls paper-fetch for search, memory and retrieval, and its domains keep only the evidence half.
